### Taxonomy Summary

| Shape | Confidence | Key Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **localized_bug_fix** | high | 20+ `bugfixes:` fragments; fork-lock, paramiko SHA2, jinja2 quote, become-loop, connection-reuse |
| **feature** | high | Vault custom salt, iptables `numeric`, cgroup v2/WSL2/Podman, sidecar module docs |
| **refactor** | high | `AnsibleJ2Vars(ChainMap)`, `_valid_attrs → fattributes + @cache` |
| **dependency_migration** | high | `resolvelib` bound, vendored `distro`, `pylint` 2.15.x, PSScriptAnalyzer 1.21.0 |
| **cleanup** | high | Removal of `cow_whitelist`, `callback_whitelist`, `forced_action_plugin` |
| **documentation/configuration** | high | Terminal commit typo; `strftime` docs; `.github/` templates |
| **test_generation** | low / ambiguous | `ansible-test` infra work present but classifies better as bug fix or feature in the test runner |
| **boilerplate** | absent | No evidence |
| **architectural_scaffolding** | absent | No evidence |

---

### Taxonomy Refinement Proposal

The existing eight categories are sufficient for this stratum with one clarification worth freezing:

> **`dependency_migration` should be split into two subtypes when applying to ansible/ansible:**
> - `dependency_migration/vendor_sync` — the vendored copy of a library is updated in-tree (e.g. `distro`, `_vendor/`). The change is entirely file content, version number, and sometimes a shim.
> - `dependency_migration/constraint_update` — the version bound in a requirements or constraints file changes without a vendor copy (e.g. `resolvelib < 0.10.0`, `wheel < 0.38.0`). The artifact is a one- or two-line file edit with no new code.

These two subtypes exhibit meaningfully different code-change shapes (large file replacement vs. single-line constraint edit) and would be misclassified as equivalent tasks by a model trained only on diff size or file count.

### Taxonomy Refinement Proposal

The existing eight categories are sufficient for this stratum with one clarification worth freezing:

> **`dependency_migration` should be split into two subtypes when applying to ansible/ansible:**
> - `dependency_migration/vendor_sync` — the vendored copy of a library is updated in-tree (e.g. `distro`, `_vendor/`). The change is entirely file content, version number, and sometimes a shim.
> - `dependency_migration/constraint_update` — the version bound in a requirements or constraints file changes without a vendor copy (e.g. `resolvelib < 0.10.0`, `wheel < 0.38.0`). The artifact is a one- or two-line file edit with no new code.

These two subtypes exhibit meaningfully different code-change shapes (large file replacement vs. single-line constraint edit) and would be misclassified as equivalent tasks by a model trained only on diff size or file count.
